jd_requirements: Designing robotic/electromechanical systems for remote handling in harsh environments
Defining architecture, specs, control logic for automated material-handling systems
Integrating automation hardware, sensors, and control systems for unmanned operations
Technical lead for automation and handling systems across lifecycle
Documentation for fabrication, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance
2D/3D CAD modeling for mechanical and robotic systems

bullets.text: Developed control programs for a six-axis CRP2 robotic arm using embedded C and ladder logic, enabling automated multi-axis motion for fuel rod testing.
Designed an STM32F103-based gateway to enable Modbus RTU communication between the PC and robotic controller, ensuring stable and real-time data exchange.

Proposed and implemented a magnetically-triggered encoder-based imaging system to replace low-precision pulse triggering, ensuring +/-1mm positional accuracy and reducing point-cloud data loss by 30%.
Integrated IR, microswitches, and pressure transducers to monitor system state and trigger safety alarms, enhancing operational reliability across the automated inspection workflow.

edits.before: Integrated sensors like IR, microswitches, and pressure transducers to monitor system state and trigger alarms. Enhanced both system operational reliability and safety.
edits.after: Integrated IR, microswitches, and pressure transducers to monitor system state and trigger safety alarms, enhancing operational reliability across the automated inspection workflow.
edits.reason: Removed vague 'sensors like' phrasing; combined two sentences into one bullet with clearer flow. Factual claim preserved.

bullets.text: Designed a compact, low-power crane system with ESP32-based Wi-Fi remote control, enabling low-latency communication and autonomous coordination across multiple devices, achieving over 95% task repeatability.
Enhanced the crane structure in SolidWorks with FEA; independently constructed STM32-based control circuitry and PCB with a stable fuzzy PID control system.

Consolidated five functional boards into a single 4-layer PCB with KiCad, integrating control, power, and communication modules; reduced overall footprint by 40% and verified signal integrity via 100-MHz oscilloscope.

Designed a modular crane prototype using aluminum profiles and sheet components, achieving 3 cost-effective iterations in 2 months with 50% faster assembly; enabled future transition to large-scale excavators.
Led a 5-member cross-functional team to develop a hybrid flying-driving robot platform, achieving 100% integration of mobility and flight subsystems.
Collaboratively designed a modular foldable robotic arm in Autodesk Fusion, reducing UAV-to-GAV transformation time by 50%.
Integrated OptiTrack motion capture system with the robotic platform, achieving <1 mm position accuracy and <10 ms latency, supporting real-time position feedback for closed-loop control.

edits.reason: Removed 'in indoor environments' to save space; factual claim preserved.

bullets.text: Spearheaded mechanical design and development of an innovative vacuum dryer system from concept to working prototype, enabling 20-minute drying at 40C with 50 dBA noise level.

Performed FMEA on the pump, heater, and motion systems under simulated drying cycles, and designed a sensor-driven control interface with built-in diagnostics to simplify operation and facilitate fault isolation.
Engineered a magnetically coupled drive system that eliminated direct mechanical interfaces, resolving vacuum leakage at drive connections and ensuring torque-stable roller actuation.

Led end-to-end mechanical development, covering CAD design, BOM planning, component selection, and supplier coordination; delivered three national-level competition robots within strict fabrication timelines.
Conducted collision analysis in Ansys to refine weld placement and fastening strategy, resulting in zero structural failures over months of intensive testing.
Applied DFM principles to CNC-machine aluminum hubs, improving alignment precision; assembled epoxy modules with mortise-and-tenon joints, boosting modularity and reducing material waste by 20%.
